caption:
Can you bring a celebrity photo to an aesthetic consultation? Yes. A reference can show a direction, but it cannot transfer bone frame, soft tissue, skin quality, or how a face moves.

A useful conversation is not “make me look like this.” It is “which proportion feels balanced, what should remain recognizably mine, and what change would still feel natural in motion?”

Save this for your consultation in Korea.

General education only.

#AestheticConsultation #NaturalLookingResults #FacialAesthetics #KoreanAesthetics #SeoulAesthetics
first_comment: If you brought one reference photo to a consultation, what exact detail would you point at — the proportion, the skin finish, or the expression? Naming it changes the whole conversation.

slides.alt_text: Slide 1 of 6: A woman at a vanity holds a printed reference photo and a hand mirror. Title: Bring the photo. Know its limits.
Slide 2 of 6: Four cards: bone frame, soft tissue, skin quality, movement. A photo cannot move a bone frame.
Slide 3 of 6: Three face outlines with the same arch drawn differently. The same feature lands differently on every face.
Slide 4 of 6: Five boxes a photo cannot show: lens distance, lighting, expression, movement, and your own anatomy.
Slide 5 of 6: Three numbered questions on balanced proportion, what stays recognizably yours, what feels natural in motion.
Slide 6 of 6: Reference sets a direction, assessment defines what translates, and the plan keeps you recognizably you.
